qc.label_under_test: A year of the 1880s or 1890s written in digits, peaking on the decade digit (18|8|x, 18|9|x, '1890s'), in any language's text, whether set off by a space or glued to its neighbours or inside program code (c.1889, in-1894, (1893), yr=1882, year = 1896). Native digits split: Arabic-Indic, Persian, Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Kannada, Myanmar and full-width digits fire about half to three-quarters as strongly, as do years written digit by digit in Chinese numerals; Thai, Lao, Telugu and Tibetan digits stay quiet (under 0.1) even in English, and Tamil, Malayalam and Khmer digits are in between (0.05-0.35). 1900-1909 fire about half as strongly, fading to 0.1-0.2 by 1907-1909; the 1870s are in between (0.13-0.47); years before 1870, 1910-2079 and earlier centuries stay quiet, in any digits and in any frame; 2080-2099 fire weakly (0.2-0.35); 1880s-90s years in words fire weakly (0.1-0.3), '89 stays quiet, era words with no such digits stay quiet. A 188x/189x code, PIN or ID in a modern setting is in between (0.1-0.3); a 188x/189x model number beside a brand or 'model' is in between but can reach 0.65; a 188x/189x count, distance, price or room number is weak (0.02-0.2) unless the text is set in the late 19th century (then 0.2-0.6), unreliable after an earlier 1850s-1870s year (up to 0.8), and 0.15-0.4 with a thousands comma (1,89x).
